questions.q: The signup_date column contains values such as 28/08/2023. Why is it safer to parse each explicit format in turn than to let pandas guess?
options: pandas cannot read dates at all
Ambiguous slash dates like 03/04/2024 could be silently read as the wrong month or day
questions.explain: A slash date can be day-first or month-first. Naming the format makes the assumption explicit and lets you test it, instead of trusting a silent guess.

questions.q: In the capstone data, 271 of the 441 slash dates have a first field above 12. What does this show?
options: The column is day-first, since a first field above 12 can only be a day
questions.explain: There is no month 13 or higher, so a first field above 12 must be a day. Since every value parses day-first, the whole column can be read that way.

questions.q: Rule 4 sets ages below 16 or above 100 to missing before imputing. Why not simply take the median of the raw column?
options: Values such as 0 and 999 would distort the median and the imputed values
The median of a column is undefined
The rule requires the mean instead
questions.explain: Impossible values are data errors, not real ages. Converting them to missing first keeps them out of the median, which is then computed from plausible ages only.

questions.q: What is the caveat about computing the median age on the whole customers table?
options: It removes the need for a test set
It uses information from every customer, so in a modeling pipeline the imputer should be fitted on training data only
questions.explain: A statistic learned from all rows includes the future test rows. The effect is small here, but a Pipeline with an imputer fitted on the training split avoids the leak.

questions.q: Why reconcile the Python features against the SQL extract?
options: Two independent implementations agreeing gives evidence that neither contains a bug, and disagreements expose hidden assumptions
questions.explain: The match on population, label, and features builds trust. The check also caught a subtle difference: pandas leaves a missing count for customers with no orders where SQL COALESCE gives zero.
